reader: AI reader 4 (targeted check of drug-checking findings, full texts read in the app's browser)

results.corrected_finding: Opioids were detected in 3.5% (34 of 972) of samples expected to be methamphetamine. Across 8,889 samples not expected to contain an illicit opioid (fentanyl, heroin or nitazene), 189 (2%) contained one, most of them (61.4%) at trace concentration (below 0.50% wt/wt).
results.locator: Abstract (Methods, Results); Methods > Inclusion criteria (collection dates, setting, 8,889 samples, trace definition); Results paragraph 1 and Table 1 (methamphetamine row: 972 samples, 34 opioid-positive, 3.5%; total row: 8,889 / 189 / 2.1% / 116 trace / 61.4%); Table 2 (methamphetamine: 903 with and 69 without the expected drug); PMC citation line (Harm Reduct J 2025 Mar 10;22:28).
results.note: Every number, the dates and the place match the paper (34/972 = 3.5%; 189/8,889; 116/189 = 61.4%; 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2023; British Columbia; published 10 March 2025). Only the wording of the denominator needed tightening: the paper's 8,889 are samples not expected to contain an 'illicit' opioid, and they include 277 samples expected to contain other opioids. The abstract gives 2% and Table 1 gives 2.1%, one Results sentence writes 8907 instead of 8889, and the article's correction footnote concerns an author name only.

results.corrected_finding: Among 103 samples bought from cryptomarkets, all 5 sold as methamphetamine (as well as all 24 sold as MDMA and all 4 sold as heroin) were found to contain only the advertised substance; the numbers are small.
results.locator: Abstract (Results); Results paragraph 1 and Table 1 (MDMA 24 of 24, methamphetamine 5 of 5, heroin 4 of 4 with only the advertised substance; total 103 / 67 / 14 / 22); Methods paragraphs 1-2 (Test4Pay posts dated 1 September 2022 to 23 August 2023; Get Your Drugs Tested in Vancouver; infrared method with 5% detection limit); page metadata (online 4 March 2024; volume 43, issue 4, pages 969-974).
results.note: The finding is right, but the full text supplies the number the abstract omits: 5 of the 103 samples were sold as methamphetamine, and all 5 contained only methamphetamine (Table 1). The where_when is correct as written. The testing method (infrared spectroscopy plus fentanyl and benzodiazepine strips) cannot reliably detect substances below 5% of the sample by weight, so 'only the advertised substance' means that no other substance was detected.

results.corrected_finding: Substitution: of the 33 samples expected to be MDMA, 10 contained no MDMA, and 3 of those 10 contained methamphetamine ('crystal Meth') instead.
results.corrected_where_when: One outdoor electronic music festival nearby Mexico City, Mexico (the paper gives no festival name, exact venue or date); 51 samples from 40 people were tested on site; published 2023
results.locator: Abstract (Methods, Results); Methods > Data collection (single festival, collection from 15:00 to 24:00, on-site testing station); Results, first subsection (51 samples from 40 participants; expected substances, MDMA 64.7%); Results > Drug checking results, subsection on adulterants (4 of 33 MDMA only, 10 without MDMA, 19 MDMA plus other substances; among the 10: 4 MDA, 3 crystal Meth, 3 no psychoactive substance), Fig. 2 and Table 4; Discussion > Study limitations (single festival); PMC citation line (Harm Reduct J 2023 Dec 6;20:174).
results.note: The finding is right, with one wording point: the paper's 33 are 'nominal MDMA' samples (what the person expected), and 3 of the 10 without MDMA had crystal Meth (4 had MDA, 3 no psychoactive substance). The paper does not state the festival's date (month or year), name or exact place, only 'nearby Mexico City' and the collection hours (15:00 to 24:00); the total tested was 51 samples from 40 people. Minor mismatch inside the paper: Table 4 gives the methamphetamine range as 14.2 to 100%, the text 14 to 62.3%, though both count 3 samples.
